query: For titanium alloys used as structural materials, formulate one hypothesis for an intervention that could increase surface hardness and wear resistance. Specify the intervention, its proposed mechanism, the expected improvement relative to the untreated alloy, the service or test conditions under which the effect should hold, prior evidence supporting the hypothesis, and a controlled experiment with clear results that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: Applying a TiN coating by physical vapor deposition (PVD) on conventional titanium alloys will increase the surface hardness and wear resistance by creating a hard nitride surface layer with compressive residual stresses.
generation.material_initial_state: A conventional titanium alloy with its typical microstructure and moderate surface hardness/wear resistance.
generation.intervention: Deposition of a thin, uniform TiN layer on the alloy surface using PVD techniques.
generation.conditions: The improvement is expected during dry sliding wear tests at room temperature under industrial service conditions, where repeated frictional contacts occur.
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of a continuous, adherent TiN phase that refines the near-surface microstructure and induces compressive residual stress.
generation.mechanism: Nitrogen reacts with surface titanium during PVD to form titanium nitride, a ceramic phase with high hardness. Concurrently, the coating process induces compressive stresses that retard crack initiation and propagation, thereby both hardening the surface and reducing wear.
generation.predicted_outcome: An approximate 40% increase in surface hardness and around a 50% decrease in wear rate compared to the untreated alloy, as evidenced by standard hardness measurements and wear testing.
generation.baseline: The untreated titanium alloy’s hardness and wear rate measured under identical test conditions.
generation.boundary: The effect is anticipated under room temperature, dry sliding conditions. At elevated temperatures or corrosive environments, the performance gains may differ.
generation.uncertainty: The exact percentage improvements depend on coating thickness, uniformity, and PVD parameters; moreover, long-term adhesion and performance under varying environmental conditions require further investigation.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two groups of samples from an identical batch of titanium alloy: one group receives the TiN coating via standardized PVD processing, and the other remains untreated. Subject both groups to a controlled pin-on-disk wear test under dry sliding conditions at room temperature for a fixed number of friction cycles. Measure the surface hardness using Vickers microhardness testing and determine the wear rate by quantifying material loss post-test.
measurements: Wear track depth and volume loss (mm3·N−1·m−1)
Residual stress analysis (if possible) via X-ray diffraction
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the TiN-coated samples do not exhibit at least a 20% increase in surface hardness and a 30% lower wear rate compared to untreated samples, the hypothesis will be considered falsified.

cited_evidence.text: One of the most investigated HEA systems is AlCoCrCuFeNi and the copper-free derivate AlCoCrFeNi [,]. Distinct improvement of mechanical properties can be achieved by alloying with titanium. Due to its large atomic radius, the addition of titanium causes solid–solution strengthening and hence increased strength and hardness. Additionally, the formation of brittle phases was observed for a high content of titanium [,,]. The wear resistance of the alloy system AlCoCrFeNiTi has been investigated under various conditions revealing an increased wear resistance, also in comparison with the steels EN 1.3505 and EN 1.3343 [,]. Although improved high-temperature properties of AlCoCrFeNiTi are expected, the wear behaviour has not yet been investigated at increased temperature.

The ceramic particle of WC is one of the most used hard phases due to its excellent properties [,]. WC is tungsten carbide which is a compound composed of tungsten and carbon with structure of hexagonal crystal. The hardness of WC is between 16 GPa and 22 GPa []. The wettability of WC with metal matrix is good. The hardening effect of WC on matrix is remarkable. On the other hand, the nailing effect produced by hard particles can limit grain growth and promote the hardness of metal matrix []. A coating of HEA reinforced with WC was prepared by plasma cladding to increase wear resistance []. The effect of WC content on microstructure and mechanical properties of composite coatings was analyzed. The results show that the existence of WC particles can effectively alleviate the wear damage of the coating and then significantly improve the wear-resistant properties of the coating. Although the addition of ceramic particles leads to an improvement of HEAs’ mechanical properties [,], the action mechanism of ceramic particles on microstructure and properties of HEAs is still not completely clear.
